items.title: Release workflow: publish evidence package from a GitHub release

items.title: Automation: document ingestion and evidence collectors
items.body:
Adds true automation on top of the GitOps engine: **client documents are drafted into the record**, and **evidence is pulled from client systems on a schedule**. Both only open PRs; nothing automated can mark a control `verified`.

### Ingestion — `intake/` → PR
- Upload client documents to `intake/` in a PR; the **Ingest** workflow commits a drafted update to that PR and comments a report.
- CSV/XLSX files matching `templates/intake/` are imported as written (no AI).
- Other documents (Word, PDF, Excel, Markdown, text) are drafted by Claude (structured output) when `ingest.ai_drafting: true` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` are set. Every item must cite its source; unknown requirement ids and unsourced items are dropped; client statements become `claimed` legs only.
- Merge is conservative: profile fields filled only if empty, gaps/evidence/inventory appended with de-duplication, comments preserved.

### Collectors — daily → "Evidence refresh" PR
- GitHub (branch protection, PR review rate, workflow runs, file presence), Drata v2 (policies, risks, vendors, training, monitoring tests), AWS/Azure/GCP config checks (OIDC, read-only).
- Snapshots in `engagement/evidence/collected/` with sha256; machine-owned index in `collected.yaml`.
- A failing check makes its evidence non-current → any leg `verified` only on it fails CI (**E015**); failing checks warn (**W108**).
- Three self-checks on this repo work with no setup (they already show that recent merges bypassed review).

Setup guide: `docs/AUTOMATION.md`. Tests: collectors and AI drafting use fakes for external APIs.

items.title: Publish browsable reports to a reports branch
items.body:
Makes every deliverable readable on GitHub without downloading a zip.

- **`publish-reports.yml`** rebuilds after every merge to `main` and daily, and commits to a **`reports`** branch. The branch isn't covered by the `main` ruleset, so no bot PRs and no merge conflicts on generated files. Its history is a dated record of readiness.
- **Landing page** (`README.md` on that branch): readiness summary + links to the brief, control matrix, SoA, gap register, evidence index (Markdown, CSV, and the Word brief).
- **Brief as Markdown** so it reads directly on GitHub.
- **Reproducible builds**: identical data → byte-identical files (incl. .docx), so the history only shows real changes.
- Repo README links to the reports branch.

items.title: Engagement ops: new-engagement, owners, evidence linking, sandbox mode
items.body:
Items 1–3 from the readiness rundown, plus sandbox mode for the pilot.

1. **New engagement** — `python -m grc new-engagement` or **Actions → New engagement**: resets `engagement/` and `intake/`, scaffolds 65 controls, computes phases from the audit dates, opens a PR.
2. **Real owners** — `engagement/owners.yaml` maps roles → GitHub users. Gap Issues are assigned, overdue gaps get one reminder per due date (sync now also runs daily), `python -m grc codeowners` makes owners required reviewers of their controls, W111 flags unknown owners.
3. **Evidence linking** — collector checks declare `supports: ["A.6.2.4:implemented"]`; the refresh PR cites passing evidence and moves not_started/claimed legs to `partial` (only if the control has an owner; never `verified`).
4. **Sandbox mode** — `sandbox: {enabled: true}` answers Drata/AWS/Azure/GCP/AI from canned files in `sandbox/`; everything is labelled [SANDBOX]. GitHub checks stay real.

55 tests (12 new).

items.title: Package the engine: thin client repos, reusable workflows, versioned upgrades
items.body:
Item A. Client repos stop carrying a copy of the engine.

- **Engine package** (v0.2.0): catalog, schemas and Word template ship inside `grc/resources/`; a client repo can override any of them by path.
- **Reusable workflows** `grc-*.yml`. This repo's own workflows now call them with the local engine (so they're exercised here); `validate.yml` stays standalone so the required `validate` check name doesn't change.
- **Versioning**: client `requirements.txt` pins `engine-vX.Y.Z`; wrappers call `@engine-v0`. **Release GRC engine** workflow tags/publishes; each client's weekly **Upgrade GRC engine** PR bumps the pin.
- **`grc bootstrap`** writes the thin client skeleton (22 files). Verified from an installed package — found and fixed packaging silently dropping `.github/`.
- Docs: `docs/ENGINE.md`. Tests: 65.

After merge: enable *Settings → Actions → General → Access → Accessible from repositories owned by the user*, then run **Release GRC engine** to publish `engine-v0.2.0`.

items.title: Engine 0.3.0: internal audit (9.2) and corrective actions (10.2)
items.body:
Item E. See `docs/AUDIT.md`.

- **Audit programme** `engagement/audit/program.yaml` → **workpapers** generated per in-scope requirement (`grc audit plan` or *Actions → Internal audit*), with test steps from intent, owner, open claims and gaps.
- **Sampling** from collector populations (merged PRs, CI runs, Drata risks/vendors) or CSV/list populations. Deterministic and re-performable: size, SHA-256 of the population and seed are recorded.
- **Rules**: auditor independence (E020), status gates (E021), workpaper conclusions incl. unexplained exceptions and self-review (E022), corrective-action lifecycle with independent effectiveness review (E024), refs (E025), open major NC vs verified *Tested* (E026), W120–W123.
- **Evidence**: a reviewed *effective* workpaper is citable test evidence (`AUD-2027-01/WP-07`).
- **Reports**: `internal-audit.md`, `audit-<ID>.md`, `corrective-actions.md/.csv`; readiness summary counts open NCs.
- **Issues**: findings → `grc-finding` Issues, assigned to owners, overdue reminders.
- New engagements start with an audit scheduled in the Test phase. Collector snapshots now include item populations.

Rehearsed on a copy of the pilot against real GitHub data (sampled 2 of the pilot's 3 merged PRs, raised NC-001). 81 tests.

After merge: run **Release GRC engine**. Client repos also need the new `.github/workflows/audit.yml` wrapper copied in once (the upgrade PR can't add workflow files).

items.title: AI system impact assessments (C) — engine 0.4.0
items.body:
Adds ISO 42001 AI system impact assessments (6.1.4, 8.4, Annex A.5.2–A.5.5). See `docs/IMPACT.md`.

- **Start:** Actions → *AI impact assessment* (`INV-001` or `all`) opens a PR with `engagement/impact/IA-NNN.yaml` for each in-scope AI system, prefilled from the inventory.
- **Method** (playbook, overridable): 11 categories across individuals, groups and society; likelihood × severity 1–5; residual ≥ 12 needs independent acceptance, ≥ 20 can't be approved; review every 180 days (High tier) or 365.
- **Gates:** E030 (references and uniqueness), E031 (complete and independently approved), E032 (residual thresholds and acceptance), W130–W133.
- **Evidence:** controls can cite `IA-001`. It counts only while approved, independently, with an approve decision, and not past review.
- **Reports:** `impact-assessments.md` plus a page per assessment; the summary shows *X of Y AI systems current and approved*.
- Fix: Word brief filename for client names with punctuation.
- Version 0.4.0. 111 tests pass, including regressions for 10 issues found by an independent review.

**After merging:** run *Release GRC engine* (0.4.0). Client repos need the new `impact.yml` wrapper added by hand, because GitHub's token can't add workflow files.

items.title: Policies and procedures as code (B) — engine 0.5.0
items.body:
Adds policies and procedures as code (item B). See `docs/DOCUMENTS.md`.

- **Library:** 17 ISO 42001 documents covering all 65 requirements exactly once, from templates in our own wording.
- **Draft:** Actions → *Policies and procedures* (`new`, `all`). Templates are filled from the engagement record: client, scope, owners, AI inventory and suppliers, plus the engine's own methods (impact scales and thresholds, audit sample sizes, the evidence test). Each owner is suggested from the controls the document supports. Anything the record can't supply stays as a `[[TODO]]`.
- **AI fill** (optional, `fill`): Claude replaces only the `[[TODO]]` markers, each with a cited source, as plain text, and only in drafts. The front matter and every other character stay unchanged. Sandbox support via `sandbox/ai_docs.json`.
- **Approve** (`approve` + approver): the command refuses unless the document has no TODOs, has its required sections, has an owner and author, and the approver isn't the author. It records a SHA-256 fingerprint of the text plus the approval details, and keeps a version history. Merging the PR is the approval.
- **Rules:** E040–E042 and W140–W143. Approved documents count as *Documented*-leg evidence. Any later edit to the text or approval details fails validation, and so does every requirement relying on it.
- **Reports:** `documents.md` register, a page per document, and a Word file per document in the house style. Word output is reproducible.
- Engine 0.5.0. 133 tests pass, including regressions for 13 issues found by an independent review.

**After merging:** release 0.5.0, then add the `docs.yml` wrapper to client repos by hand (GitHub's token can't add workflow files).

items.title: Management review (F) — engine 0.6.0
items.body:
Adds management review (ISO 42001 9.3), item F. See `docs/REVIEW.md`.

- **Schedule:** Actions → *Management review* (`new` + date). A new engagement schedules its first review before Stage 1.
- **Input pack:** `pack` + review id generates the pack from the record, one section per required input:
  - previous actions
  - context changes and documents approved since the last review
  - interested parties
  - performance: readiness, nonconformities, failing checks, audit results
  - risks and impact assessments
  - improvement: open OFIs and documents not yet approved
  - resources

  The pack is frozen with a SHA-256 once the review is held. It's in Markdown and Word.
- **Minutes:** CI blocks a review recorded as held unless it has a date, chair, attendees, notes for every input, at least one decision, and an intact pack prepared before the meeting. Closing it also needs approved minutes and no open actions.
- **Actions** become GitHub Issues (`grc-review-action`), assigned to their owners, with overdue reminders.
- **Evidence:** a held review with approved minutes can be cited (`MR-2027-01`), for example on 9.3.
- **Rules:** E050–E052 and W150–W153 (overdue review, none held before Stage 1, overdue action, 9.3 verified without a review).
- Also: clearer error when a document's approver is the same person as its author.
- Engine 0.6.0. 150 tests pass, including regressions for 6 issues found by an independent review.

**After merging:** release 0.6.0, then add the `review.yml` wrapper to client repos by hand. Optionally add `engagement/reviews/**` to the client's `sync-issues.yml` paths; the daily schedule picks actions up anyway.

items.title: More evidence collectors (D) — engine 0.7.0
items.body:
Adds more evidence sources (item D). See *Evidence collection* in `docs/AUTOMATION.md`.

| Collector | Proves | Credentials |
|---|---|---|
| `jira.issues` | A ticket-based process operates, from a JQL query: minimum count, assignees, required fields (e.g. an approval field), no stale open tickets, resolved within N days. Works for AI incidents, change requests, release approvals and concerns. | `JIRA_BASE_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL` (variables), `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (secret) |
| `sharepoint.documents` | Named documents exist in a library folder, changed within N days, latest version published (x.0) | `MS_TENANT_ID`, `MS_CLIENT_ID` (variables), `MS_CLIENT_SECRET` (secret); Graph `Sites.Read.All` |
| `gdrive.documents` | Same for a Google Drive folder or shared drive | Existing GCP workload-identity sign-in |
| `aws.sagemaker_model_registry` | Latest version Approved, no stale pending approvals, approver ≠ creator, model card attached | Existing AWS OIDC role |

- Every collector lists the items it checked, so they can become the population an internal audit samples (for example, Jira ticket keys or approved model versions).
- **Sandbox:** canned responses come from `sandbox/http.yaml` (and `aws.yaml` for SageMaker). In sandbox mode, these services are never called for real. GitHub is still called for real, as before.
- Snapshots record metadata only. No document content, and no identities from model registries.
- Engine 0.7.0. 162 tests pass, including regressions for the issues found by an independent review (3 bugs and several robustness gaps).

items.title: Auditor package (G) — engine 0.8.0
items.body:
Adds the auditor package (item G). See `docs/AUDITOR-PACKAGE.md`.

**Command:** `grc package --label stage1`. A release now runs it automatically and attaches the zip and the auditor index PDF.

**What's in the package:**
- Every report as PDF, organised by audit area: overview, applicability, documented information, risk and impact, evidence, internal audit, management review. PDFs are rendered in pure Python (ReportLab), so CI needs no office software.
- Word copies of the brief, the policies and procedures, and the review packs.
- Collector snapshots, and the source record (tracked files only).
- **Auditor index**, which contains:
  - engagement facts and source commit
  - how to read the evidence test
  - readiness at a glance
  - **requirement → evidence traceability** for every leg, with where each cited item is (in the package, or where the client holds it)
  - known issues at packaging
  - every file's SHA-256
- `manifest.json`, `SHA256SUMS` and a **reproducible zip**: the same commit, as-of date and versions give the same bytes.

**Safeguards:**
- It refuses an invalid record unless `--force`.
- The commit is marked `-dirty` if the engagement folder has uncommitted changes.
- Nothing in the output folder changes unless the whole package succeeds.

Engine 0.8.0, with the new dependency `reportlab`. 172 tests pass, including regressions for 10 issues found by an independent review.

items.title: Hours tracking (H) — engine 0.9.0
items.body:
Adds hours tracking (item H). See `docs/HOURS.md`.

- **Timesheet** in `engagement/hours.yaml`. Hours used, burn by phase, activity, person and week, and a forecast are all computed from it. The hand-typed `budget.hours_used` is no longer needed; W163 flags it if it's left in and disagrees.
- **Import:** drop Toggl, Harvest or Clockify exports (or any CSV with date and hours) into `intake/timesheets/` and push. A *Timesheet update* PR follows.
  - `HOURS_MATCH` keeps only this client's rows.

  - Re-importing renamed or cumulative exports never double-counts.
  - Ambiguous day/month dates are flagged.
- **Log:** Actions → *Hours* → `log` records a single entry (hours, activity, note, references; you are the person).
- **Plans:** hours per phase, set explicitly or from the playbook split of the budget.
- **Rules:** E060 (invalid entries, more than 14 h per person per day), W106 (80% of budget, now from the timesheet), W160 (phase over plan), W161 (forecast over budget), W163.
- **Reports:** `hours.md` and `hours.csv`. The summary and brief show hours used. The timesheet is **not** included in the auditor package.
- New engagements start with an empty timesheet.
- Engine 0.9.0. 185 tests pass, including regressions for 7 bugs and several design changes from an independent review.

**After merging:** release 0.9.0, then add the `hours.yml` wrapper to client repos by hand.

items.title: Client site: readiness portal; answers arrive as reviewed PRs (engine 0.12.0)
items.body:
Adds the **client site**: a small website where the client's people see their readiness and answer requests. It is engine 0.12.0.

## What clients see
- **Overview:** days to the Stage 1 audit, open requests, a "path to certification" timeline, the next four requests, key figures.
- **Requests:** grouped by when they're due and filterable by person. Each one has "what we need", "why this matters" and "what good evidence looks like", plus a short answer form (text, up to 5 links, and a confirmation that there's no patient or personal data).
- **Progress:** each area of the standard with done / under way / not started bars, and an optional technical layer showing requirement numbers and the four evidence checks.
- **Help:** each term in plain language, with the technical term underneath.
- More than one framework shows as tabs (`grc portal --also <dir>`), ready for ISO 27001.

## How answers flow
- A client's answer becomes a **pull request** adding `engagement/submissions/SUB-….yaml`.
- The analyst reviews it, then sets `accepted`, `needs_more` (with a note the client sees) or `withdrawn`, and merges.
- A submission **never changes a control, gap or evidence status**.
- New checks:
  - **E070:** id/file mismatch
  - **W171:** waiting for review longer than `triage_days`
  - **W172:** unknown evidence id
  - **W170:** answer to a request that is no longer open (info)
- `submissions.md` is the analyst's queue. It is excluded from the auditor package.

## Security
- A Cloudflare Worker sits behind Cloudflare Access. The Worker checks the Access login itself, on pages too, and **refuses everyone if the login isn't configured**.
- Answers use a fine-grained GitHub token limited to this one repository.
- Requests must be same-origin JSON. Input is cleaned, and there are rate limits.
- There are no uploads (clients share links instead) and no third-party code; the site runs under a strict content-security policy.
- An independent review found no way around the login and no

items.body:
Adds the **user manual** in `docs/manual/`, versioned with the engine. It has three parts:

Inside the package, the brief and status summary omit hours and budget, and budget warnings are left out of the known issues.
- **Management review packs showed consulting hours**, and from a deprecated field. That line is removed.
- **Invalid YAML in a control, gap or evidence file crashed validation** with a Python traceback. It now stops with one clear line naming the file, the line number and what to check.

items.body:
Adds **ISO/IEC 27001:2022** and lets one client repository hold one record per framework, with reviewed cross-framework reuse. Engine version **0.13.0**.

## ISO 27001
- **Catalog:** 25 clauses and 93 Annex A controls (A.5 ×37, A.6 ×8, A.7 ×14, A.8 ×34). The intents and evidence examples are our own paraphrase.
- **Playbook:** phases, readiness criteria, the ISO 27001 management review inputs, and no AI impact assessments.
- **ISMS document library:** 20 templates, covering every clause and control exactly once. Examples: Information Security Policy, Risk Management with the SoA, Access Control, Supplier and Cloud, Incident, Continuity, Operations, Secure Development.
- **Framework-neutral engine:** the brief, review pack, client view and site, auditor index, workbook, issue text, new-engagement audit programme and AI prompts now take the framework's name and AIMS/ISMS.

## Two records in one repository (`engagement/` + `engagement-27001/`)
- **`grc engagements`** lists the records. It fails loudly if there are none, or if a record is misnamed, incomplete or duplicated.
- **Workflows that cover every record:** validate, publish reports, collect, freshness, sync issues and release all loop over the records.
- **Workflows you run by hand** take an **engagement** input: audit, documents, review, impact and new engagement. The input is checked, and branch names get the record's suffix.
- **New engagement** takes **framework** and **engagement** inputs. A second record gets its own intake folder; the main record is never touched.
- **GitHub Issues:** a second record's issues are marked `iso27001:GAP-01`, titled `[ISO 27001]`, with their own milestones.
- **Reports:** the second record's reports go in a subfolder, linked from the main landing page.
- **Client site:** each record becomes a tab automatically.

## Cross-framework reuse

items.title: SOC 2 framework (engine 0.14.0)
items.body:
Adds **SOC 2** (AICPA Trust Services Criteria) as the third built-in framework, and makes the engine's wording framework-neutral so SOC 2 records don't show ISO terms. Engine version 0.14.0.

## SOC 2
- **Catalog** (`frameworks/soc2/catalog.yaml`): all 61 criteria in our own words (33 common criteria + Availability 3, Confidentiality 2, Processing Integrity 5, Privacy 18). No AICPA text reproduced.
- **Categories**: Security always; the others chosen per record (`scope.categories`, `new-engagement --categories`, or the new *categories* workflow input). Criteria outside the chosen categories drop out of assessment files, requests, reports, documents, metrics and mappings. Unknown category: **E016**. Open gap only about removed categories: **W112**.
- **Playbook**: phases from scoping through readiness assessment to the observation period; `terms:` (observation period start/end, service auditor, *Criteria Applicability*, CC4.1/CC4.2/CC1.2 references) and a SOC 2 Help glossary (Type 1/2, observation period, carve-out, exceptions).
- **Library**: 18 policy/procedure templates covering every criterion once; documents for categories not chosen aren't required.
- **Mapping** `mappings/iso27001__soc2.yaml`: proposed, 4 equivalent, 2 subset, 1 superset, 42 related.

## Engine changes for any framework
- Catalog `kinds:` / `categories:`, playbook `terms:` / `glossary:`; ISO wording is the default, so ISO records are unchanged (tests check this).
- Client site: progress headings, countdown, Help references and glossary come from the framework.
- Management review pack inputs can reuse built-in sections (`content:`); timesheet import recognises SOC 2 ids.

- Independent review done; all findings fixed (second commit).
- Docs: `docs/FRAMEWORKS.md`, README, manual (Frameworks section, codes, T-31).
